title: Streamline interop checker & golden-seed harness for streaming + tool calls
creator: Alejandra Cruz
description: Build a reusable harness that validates multi-mode API behavior (streaming tokens, interleaved tool/function calls, and structured output schemas) against a stable set of golden seeds. The goal is a low-flakiness CI gate that exercises edgecases (token-boundary splits, incremental JSON emissions, tool-call interleavings) and provides deterministic fingerprints for regressions across runtime and model variants.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible harness (python + node runner) that can run N golden seeds and produce deterministic fingerprints for: token stream order, tool call invocation sequence, and final structured payloads
CI job in buildkite that runs the harness on PRs touching streaming/tool code and fails on fingerprint diffs
An initial canonical golden set of 120 seeds covering: typical chat flows, function-call heavy conversations, partial JSON emits, and KV-cache priming scenarios
Failure triage dashboard (Grafana) linked from CI showing diff types and top 10 failing seeds
Documentation and runbook for adding new golden seeds including anti-flakiness guidelines
proposed_solution: Create a dual-language harness: a lightweight python runner for local dev and a node-based executor used in CI that mirrors production streaming behavior. Each golden seed will include a canonical prompt, expected stream events (ndjson-like events), and a fingerprint script that hashes event canonicalization. The runner will support: simulated network chunking, controlled latency, stubbed tool endpoints, and KV-cache priming to reproduce timing-sensitive cases.
implementation_notes: Runner libraries: use existing stream-compat client (internal npm package) to deserialize events
Fingerprint format: canonicalize by stripping ids/timestamps then sha256 of newline-joined event types + relevant fields
Tool stubs: docker-based lightweight HTTP stubs used in CI; local dev can use --stubbed flag to run in-process
Seed format: newline-delimited json file per seed with metadata header describing expected modality (stream|tool|structured), modeled latency profile, and run tags
Flake mitigations: run 3-sample median of fingerprints in CI, persist last-known-good fingerprint per branch for easier bisecting
test_plan: Create 120 initial golden seeds across categories: 40 streaming-only, 40 tool-heavy, 20 structured-output edgecases, 20 KV-cache and sequence-sensitivity
Unit tests for the fingerprinting canonicalizer (target 95% coverage)
Integration smoke in CI: short-run (20 seeds) on PRs, full-run nightly (120 seeds) with diff alerting
Add negative tests for malformed ndjson fragments and tool reentrancy
Include a synthetic determinism test that toggles model quantization flags to detect kernel-level non-determinism
ci_jobs: buildkite/api-stream-harness-smoke: runs 20 quick seeds on PRs (15m)
buildkite/compat-fingerprint-bisect: helper job triggered when nightly fails to collect artifacts and run bisect scripts
ci/flake-cleaner: scheduled job that re-runs failed seeds 2x to reduce false positives
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): land harness + 20 seed canonical set, iterate with developers for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (CI): enable PR smoke job and surface failures as soft alerts for a week
Phase 3 (blocker): flip PR smoke to hard-fail on deterministic mismatches after investigating top flakiness causes
Phase 4 (nightly): enable full nightly run and wire Grafana alerting to oncall
metrics: Golden-flip rate: fraction of seeds whose fingerprint changes vs baseline (daily)
PR-block rate: number of PRs blocked by harness on first run
Flake rate: percent of harness failures that are resolved by re-run
Time-to-investigation: median time from failed seed to triage ticket creation
risks: False positives due to non-deterministic kernels or hardware differences across CI runners
High runtime cost for nightly full-run if run on GPU-backed model variants
Complexity of maintaining seed corpus as protocol/features evolve
Potential for harness to mask real regressions if canonicalizer over-normalizes outputs
